request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added sign-in by name and loading a sheet by id, and the Playwright test now passes with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works on screen:** a session bar sits in the app shell above the page, so it shows on `/`.
- **Signing in:** before signing in you see a name field (`signin-name`) and a Sign in button (`signin-submit`). Once signed in, your name shows in `current-user`.
- **Loading a sheet:** after signing in you get a sheet-id field (`sheet-id-input`) and a Load sheet button (`sheet-load`). The active sheet id shows in `sheet-current-id`.
- **Errors:** a blank name or a bad sheet id shows an error (`signin-error`, `sheet-load-error`). The error clears as soon as you edit the form or submit again. The test doesn't name these two error ids, so I chose them. I didn't call the second one `sheet-error` because the test helpers already use that name for other sheet actions, like archiving.

**Stored data and server:**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V1__sheet.sql`, adds a `sheet` table that records each sheet's id, who created it and when.
- **Sign-in:** `POST /api/session` checks the name isn't blank and sends it back trimmed. There's no password. The browser keeps the name and sends it on later requests in an `X-User` header.
- **Loading:** `POST /api/sheets/load` reads the sheet from the store each time, and creates it empty the first time an id is used. If two users create the same sheet at the same moment, both end up with the one sheet.
- **Front end:** a shared `Session` service (`core/session.ts`) holds the signed-in name and the active sheet id, so later features can keep their data per sheet.

The test doesn't expect any audit records for this change, so nothing is written to the audit file. I didn't edit the test, `bin/*`, `e2e/support/*` or the instruction files.
